transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-12-09 15:00 PST | Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Head of ML, Stratus), Carlos Ruiz (CTO, Stratus), Ibrahim Khan (SRE, Stratus)

Summary: Quick discovery to understand Stratus Labs' model needs: they ingest long legal and engineering docs, need multilingual support across EN/ES/FR/DE, want tool-calling to internal search and ticketing, and are evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated for cost/latency and Private for data residency.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya: good, thanks. we have about an hour, want to go over our setup and what we're evaluating.
[00:12] Carlos: yeah, quick agenda, our needs, what you provide, and then deep into model choices.
[00:18] Priya: great, we'll do high level then technical. feel free to interrupt.
[00:25] Jordan: can we start with current stack? what are you using today for models?
[00:30] Maya: mostly OpenAI API, chat completions for support summarization and internal Q&A, some homegrown infra for embeddings with faiss. but costs are getting high with 8k context jobs and we have privacy concerns.
[00:42] Carlos: also latency spikes are painful when concurrent users hit the system during daytime.
[00:48] Ibrahim: and we have a compliance push, need audit logs and KMS integration for keys at rest.
[00:54] Priya: ok that helps. how about scale and context length? you mentioned 8k, any longer needs?
[01:00] Maya: yes, we're piloting a docs ingestion feature requiring 50k-100k token contexts for whole doc summarization and question answering. realistic envelope is 64k average, some up to 100k.
[01:12] Jordan: good to know. Redwood supports variable context via model variants and we have optimized kernels for longer seqs; for Hosted we offer model catalog entries with performance profiles; Dedicated gives predictability for throughput; Private if you need on-prem or strict network isolation.
[01:26] Carlos: on model selection, we like open models. can you compare Redwood supported open models? i saw mention of LlamaX, Falcon, Mistral in your docs.
[01:36] Priya: sure, briefly: we surface curated open models in our catalog. Falcon-based variants are strong for throughput and cost, Llama-derived models often give better instruction-following, and some newer Mistral-family models have excellent multilingual capabilities. quantization options and kernel selection change latency and memory. also the longer context variants we expect to use are often custom configs — we can run benchmarks on your workload.
[01:55] Maya: multilingual is big for us - Spanish and French support must be near parity with English. any model recommendations?
[02:02] Priya: for multilingual, Mistral-family and some of the recent Llama variants that are fine-tuned for multilingual are good. we also have curated test sets to show BLEU/accuracy across EN/ES/FR. depending on tolerance you might pick a model with stronger baseline multilingual but slightly higher cost.
[02:16] Ibrahim: what's the function-calling story? we need tool-calling to our internal search and to create tickets in JIRA.
[02:23] Priya: Redwood supports structured tool-calling patterns; we expose a function-calling interface similar to what devs expect: you can register tools, we surface JSON schema styles, and the runtime handles streaming responses while maintaining call state. Hosted supports it today, Dedicated/Private can integrate with internal network endpoints via secure routing.
[02:40] Carlos: any limits on outbound calls from Private? we need to keep endpoints internal only.
[02:45] Jordan: Private deployment supports customer-managed networking so all calls stay in your VPC/on-prem. Dedicated can be configured with private peering too.
[02:52] Maya: curious about latency targets: we aim for median token latency under 200ms for interactive QA. is that realistic?
[02:59] Priya: it depends on model size and quantization. with optimized kernels and batching, for medium-sized models and Dedicated capacity you can hit sub-200ms medians for typical prompts; Hosted SLAs vary by tier. part of the POC we'll measure with your prompt distribution.
[03:15] Ibrahim: how do you handle KV cache and reuse for long context? we have many repeated prefixes.
[03:20] Priya: we do KV cache management and prefix caching; Redwood's runtime can cache commonly seen prefixes and reuse KV to reduce compute. for very long contexts we usually recommend chunked retrieval with a retrieval-augmented approach, or using longer-context model variants where appropriate.
[03:35] Carlos: on cost, any ballpark for 64k contexts?
[03:39] Jordan: ballpark varies a lot by model and quantization; we'll include example unit economics in the pricing worksheet but expect Dedicated to reduce unit cost if you have predictable throughput. we'll add a sample calc for your traffic.
[03:51] Maya: security items - SOC 2, SSO, RBAC, KMS. do you have SOC 2?
[03:56] Jordan: yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; we can share the compliance pack. we integrate with customer KMS for Private or Dedicated; Hosted can integrate with customer-managed keys in some cases, or we can offer encryption at rest with our keys and provide audit logs.
[04:14] Ibrahim: for data residency, we need EU-only processing for a subset of customers.
[04:19] Priya: we have regional routing and Private deployments allow EU-only processing; for Hosted we can pin region for certain workloads, but for strict legal controls Private is recommended.
[04:29] Carlos: can we do a quick sketch of an architecture for our POC?
[04:33] Priya: yes, suggested: ingest pipeline -> embedding store (faiss) -> Redwood endpoint for generation and function-calling -> backend worker for tickets and search. For Dedicated POC, we'd provision a GPU pool sized for your concurrency and run benchmarks with your sample prompts.
[04:51] Maya: perfect. next, model tradeoffs - when to pick Hosted open model vs Dedicated private model?
[04:57] Jordan: Hosted is fastest to iterate and lower upfront; Dedicated reduces per-token cost and gives predictable latency; Private is for strict compliance or data residency. Often teams start on Hosted to validate and move to Dedicated or Private for production. We'll recommend based on your cost and latency thresholds.
[05:12] Maya: about tool-calling reliability - if the model calls our ticketing endpoint and the endpoint fails, what's the fallback?
[05:19] Priya: Redwood has retry/fallback policies and can optionally store the call payload for later replay. You can implement idempotency so retries are safe. We can also configure circuit-breakers.
[05:31] Ibrahim: we need to run a benchmark — typical throughput will be 200 concurrent users, average prompt 1k tokens, with occasional 50k context jobs.
[05:41] Priya: good detail. we'll size Dedicated nodes for that concurrency and include burst policies.
[05:47] Carlos: any mention of model eval tooling? we want to track hallucination/regression across rollouts.
[05:53] Jordan: Redwood Optimize has eval hooks and quality monitoring; you can bind prompt sets and get regression alerts during rollouts. We'll show that in the deep-dive.
[06:03] Maya: timeline - we need a vendor decision by end of Q1. we'd like a POC in Jan.
[06:09] Jordan: that's doable. action items we'll capture.
[06:13] Priya: technical questions - what quantization support do you have for very long context models?
[06:18] Priya: we support 4-bit and some optimized 2-bit quant paths depending on model family. there are tradeoffs with quality on certain tasks; we'll run A/B to measure.
[06:29] Maya: do you host models like Llama 3 or Mistral 2?
[06:33] Jordan: we host a combination of community and curated variants; we can bring Llama-family models and Mistral-family models, and often provide tuned variants for chat and tool-calling.
[06:43] Carlos: sample prompts: we will provide a set of 30 golden prompts including multilingual cases.
[06:48] Maya: and we will include legal docs for long context tests.
[06:52] Jordan: great. we'll use those for benchmark runs.
[06:56] Ibrahim: any constraints on embedding dimension choices? we have a legacy 1536-dim index.
[07:01] Priya: Redwood supports multiple embedding models and dimensions; we can map to your index or run remapping during the POC.
[07:08] Maya: can you explain fallback routing if a model is overloaded? we need graceful degradation.
[07:14] Priya: we support policy-based routing: latency-first or cost-first. if a preferred model is overloaded we can route to a compatible variant or lower-cost alternative and annotate responses.
[07:27] Carlos: how transparent are cost and token breakdowns?
[07:31] Jordan: Console shows token-level cost and latency breakdown per route and per API key. You'll get visibility into which prompts cost the most.
[07:40] Maya: what about retention and logs for compliance? we need 7 years of audit events for certain flows.
[07:47] Jordan: we can export audit logs to your SIEM and support long retention in Private; Hosted retention can be configured but may need an add-on.
[07:57] Ibrahim: we keep hitting sequence length limits in other vendors. you'll let us test realistic 100k context jobs?
[08:03] Priya: yes, as part of the POC we'll provision a long-context model variant and measure memory and tail latencies. note that for huge contexts we usually recommend retrieval-based chunking to reduce cost.
[08:16] Maya: what about multilingual fine-tuning? we may want to fine-tune a model on our domain.
[08:21] Jordan: Redwood supports custom fine-tuning workflows for Dedicated and Private; Hosted can support hosted fine-tuning where feasible. we'll outline options.
[08:31] Carlos: any concern about model IP or license for open models?
[08:35] Priya: we keep track of license compatibility in our model catalog and advise accordingly. for restricted licenses we may not host certain variants, but we can support customer-provided models in Private.
[08:47] Maya: ok let's recap next steps.
[08:50] Jordan: recap: 1) Jordan to send Dedicated sizing and pricing worksheet and SOC 2/KMS docs by 12/12. 2) Priya to schedule technical deep-dive and benchmark execution with Ibrahim and Carlos for week of 12/15. 3) Maya to send sample prompts, multilingual corpus, and long docs by 12/11. 4) Redwood to prepare an initial model shortlist and benchmark plan.
[09:15] Carlos: that works. one more question: for function-calling, can we get schema validation on the model output?
[09:22] Priya: yes we validate against JSON schema and can fail-safe if output doesn't validate. We can also emit confidence metrics.
[09:31] Ibrahim: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll expect the materials.
[09:34] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email.

Notes: minor transcription errors present - product names like Mistral/Mistral-X might be interchanged; Llama variants abbreviated. References to pricing are approximate and will be confirmed in worksheet.

End of transcript.
